newsitem.title: USA: Christopher to resign soon - U.S. officials.
newsitem.headline: Christopher to resign soon - U.S. officials.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher is expected to resign in the next few days but will remain in his post through President Bill Clinton's inauguration in January, U.S. officials said on Wednesday.
"I'm sure he will resign...in the next few days," one official told Reuters.
Officials said that Christopher, who has a heavy schedule of commitments over the next two months, would continue in his post until Clinton was sworn in for a second term on Jan. 20.
Christopher discussed his plans with Clinton on Tuesday in Little Rock, Arkansas, the hometown of the president, who was there for his election night victory celebration.

U.N. Ambassador Madeleine Albright and former Senate Majority Leader George Mitchell are considered leading candidates to succeed him. Some officials say Mitchell has an edge after helping Clinton prepare for election debates.

Insiders have not ruled out former Bosnia peacemaker Richard Holbrooke, Democratic Sen. Sam Nunn of Georgia or a Republican, like Sen. Richard Lugar of Indiana, who could help negotiate with the Republican-controlled Congress on Clinton's foreign policy agenda.
